passages.title: Passage I (Questions 111–115)
passages.body: What is truth? said jesting Pilate, and would not stay for an answer. Certainly there be, that delight in giddiness, and count it a bondage to fix a belief; affecting free-will in thinking, as well as in acting. And though the sects of philosophers of that kind be gone, yet there remain certain discoursing wits, which are of the same veins, though there be not so much blood in them, as was in those of the ancients. But it is not only the difficulty and labour, which men take in finding out of truth, nor again, that when it is found, it imposeth upon man’s thoughts, that doth bring lies in favour; but a natural though corrupt love of the lie itself. One of the later school of the Grecians, examineth matter, and is at a stand to think what should be in it, that men should love lies; where neither they make for pleasure as with poets, nor for advantage, as with the merchants; but for the lie’s sake. But I cannot tell; this same truth, is a naked, and open day-light, that doth not show the masks, and mummeries, and triumphs, of the world, half so stately and daintily as candle-lights. Truth may perhaps come to the price of a pearl, that showeth best by day; but it will not rise to the price of a diamond, or carbuncle, that showeth best in varied lights. A mixture of a lie doth ever add pleasure. Doth any man doubt, that if there were taken out of men’s minds, vain opinions, flattering hopes, false valuations, imaginations as one would, and the like, but it would leave the minds, of a number of men, poor shrunken things, full of melancholy and indisposition, and unpleasing to themselves?
passages.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

passages.title: Passage II (Questions 116–120)
passages.body: The ‘law’ is an enterprise that seeks to rule us all from cradle to the grave, whether as constitution confronting custom, or as custom confronting constitution, and often indeed as the diverse combinatory prowess of both. The very notion of enterprise suggests risk-taking i.e., risk as a site for both opportunity as well as failure for regulation or felicitation of approved social conduct. At the same moment, this coupling of the constitutional and custom is at the outset designed to pluralise the notion of legal literacy, a message yet to be fully constructed and conveyed co-equally to those who govern us and those who would resist domination. As citizens, we are supposed to know the law made by the state, whether we intend to obey it or break it. As members of cultural and religious communities, we also need to know the norms that define our membership of these collectives. Often, our identity and obligations as members of a political society and of diverse memberships within cultural and religious communities constitute spheres of peaceful coexistence. Often, too these collide. To decide what obligations ought to have precedence, each one of us in collision situations has to know a great deal about the law of the state and that constituting community and identity other than the political. Literacy in state law is important but never enough for an understanding of multiple sources of obligations that constantly press upon us. This invites engagement with many difficult questions including what we may want to mean by literacy, law, domination, and resistance. Further, the question always is: how far do resources of legal literacy endow us with resources of justice for all and care of self and care for others?
passages.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

passages.title: Cloze passage (Questions 81–90)
passages.body: Objectives, ideology, programmes, leadership, and organisation are important (81) _____ of social movements. They are interdependent, (82) _____ each other. The objectives of the movement change from (83) _____ particular local issues to broad aims (84) _____ social transformation. Sometimes a movement which begins with broad objectives may in the process get (85) _____ with one or two particular issues. Ideology also (86) _____ change. It provides direction for evolving strategies and programmes; and also keeps the participants together by developing feelings of ‘we-ness’. Various strategies and programmes are evolved to (87) _____ the people. They (88) _____ the movement for a long period. Leadership (89) _____ initiates or emerges in the course of the growth of the movement plays a crucial role in (90) _____ ideology and objectives, evolving strategies and programmes and maintaining the spirit of the participant.
passages.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

The artist __pranced__ around the stage singing enthusiastically.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Pranced' is the action done by the artist, so it is a verb.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

Put the fork and knife __in__ the cutlery box.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'In' shows the position relative to 'the cutlery box', so it is a preposition.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

She came __slowly__ up to the main door.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Slowly' tells how she came, so it is an adverb.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__Oh no!__ I am getting late for the function.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Oh no!' is an exclamation of sudden feeling, so it is an interjection.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

__They__ are all going to attend the function.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'They' stands in place of a noun, so it is a pronoun.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

The sun shone through the __dull__ grey clouds.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Dull' describes the noun 'clouds', so it is an adjective.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

The Principal is presiding __over__ the meeting.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Over' links 'presiding' to 'the meeting' (the verb 'preside over'), so it is a preposition.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

Cash machines __permit__ people to withdraw money at any time.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Permit' is the action of the subject 'machines', so it is a verb.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

The novel is __loosely__ based on his childhood in England.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Loosely' modifies the participle 'based', so it is an adverb.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find which part of speech the underlined word or phrase belongs to.

Since children have so much homework to do their __playtime__ is very limited.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Part of speech depends on the job a word does in the sentence.
Step 1: 'Playtime' names a period of time and is the subject of 'is', so it is a noun.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Another version of the play based on the text was re-enacted successfully after the prosecution and eventual ______ of enacting the play in public theatre by the Government.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: The government banned the play, so the noun is 'proscription' (a ban).
Step 2: 'Prescription' means a doctor's order; 'proscribing' is not a noun after 'eventual'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Ravi remembers the year when there was a ______ flood.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: An adjective is needed before 'flood'; 'devastating' fits a harmful flood.
Step 2: 'Salubrious' (healthy) and 'ameliorative' (improving) do not fit.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Davis is not sure whether he should ______ the forest guest house after dark.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: After 'should' the base verb is needed, which excludes 'left' and 'leaves'.
Step 2: 'Leave the guest house after dark' takes a direct object; 'stay the guest house' would need 'at'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

They ______ as responsible people do during the difficult situation.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: The subject 'They' is plural and the clause needs a finite past verb: 'behaved'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Criminal law has taken long ______ in facilitating access to justice for women by making various provisions.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Take long strides' means to make great progress.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Many laws have been made to deal with the problems of ______ against women.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Offences against women' is the natural phrase for crimes committed against them.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

A person purchasing goods and services for commercial purposes will also not come under the ______ of this act.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Come under the purview of' an act means to fall within its scope.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

The emergence of a sovereign Indian nation was ______ on the notion of equality.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Premised on' means based on. 'Depend' is not a participle here.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

In Manipur, the most important piece of literary work that continues to ______ a sense of patriotism is ‘Khongjom Parva’.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: After 'continues to' the base verb is needed. 'Instil a sense of patriotism' is the collocation; 'install' means to fit equipment.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

Women’s autobiographies in the post-Independence period can be seen as ______ of their literary interest.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Evidence of their literary interest' makes sense: the autobiographies show that interest.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Rearrange the jumbled parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.

P: was gradually engulfing the society with its concomitant
Q: one could not overlook the diminishing religiosity which
R: while plays with mythological content continued to be in vogue
S: implication for the stage from the third decade of the twentieth century
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the subject, then the verb, then the rest.
Step 1: Join the parts to read: 'One could not overlook the diminishing religiosity which was gradually engulfing the society with its concomitant implication for the stage from the third decade of the twentieth century while plays with mythological content continued to be in vogue.'.
Answer: (c) QPSR.
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Rearrange the jumbled parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.

P: defends private property, emphasizes the virtues of competition
Q: but also as an ideology in its own right, specifically one that
R: and suggests that general prosperity will result from the pursuit of self-interest
S: capitalism, for instance, is sometimes treated not merely as an economic system
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the subject, then the verb, then the rest.
Step 1: Join the parts to read: 'Capitalism, for instance, is sometimes treated not merely as an economic system but also as an ideology in its own right, specifically one that defends private property, emphasizes the virtues of competition and suggests that general prosperity will result from the pursuit of self-interest.'.
Answer: (c) SQPR.
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Rearrange the jumbled parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.

P: the equality provisions in the Constitution
Q: nor are they confined to individuals as bearers of rights
R: are not merely anti-discriminatory, based on the assumption of neutrality
S: of the state towards all citizens
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the subject, then the verb, then the rest.
Step 1: Join the parts to read: 'The equality provisions in the Constitution are not merely anti-discriminatory, based on the assumption of neutrality of the state towards all citizens nor are they confined to individuals as bearers of rights.'.
Answer: (a) PRSQ.
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Rearrange the jumbled parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.

P: learning-teaching process continued seamlessly
Q: but it took it in its stride, pulling through enough
R: innovations to ensure that the
S: the pandemic year was a challenge for the university
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the subject, then the verb, then the rest.
Step 1: Join the parts to read: 'The pandemic year was a challenge for the university but it took it in its stride, pulling through enough innovations to ensure that the learning-teaching process continued seamlessly.'.
Answer: (c) SQRP.
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Rearrange the jumbled parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.

P: proscribed at the slightest hint of any seditious intent
Q: the Dramatic Performances Act effectively marked the end of direct
R: political activism what little had been demonstrated
S: in the Bengali public theatre although some plays continued to be
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the subject, then the verb, then the rest.
Step 1: Join the parts to read: 'The Dramatic Performances Act effectively marked the end of direct political activism what little had been demonstrated in the Bengali public theatre although some plays continued to be proscribed at the slightest hint of any seditious intent.'.
Answer: (d) QRSP.
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Rearrange the jumbled parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.

P: moderation and compromise may mean that multiparty
Q: a final problem is that the tendency towards
R: are unable to offer clear ideological alternatives
S: systems are so dominated by the political centre that they
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the subject, then the verb, then the rest.
Step 1: Join the parts to read: 'A final problem is that the tendency towards moderation and compromise may mean that multiparty systems are so dominated by the political centre that they are unable to offer clear ideological alternatives.'.
Answer: (b) QPSR.
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Rearrange the jumbled parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.

P: even after an offence has been committed
Q: provisions for women still is dependent on the observations
R: of the rules of procedure and evidence by the implementing agencies
S: the criminal justice administration with all its favourable
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the subject, then the verb, then the rest.
Step 1: Join the parts to read: 'The criminal justice administration with all its favourable provisions for women still is dependent on the observations of the rules of procedure and evidence by the implementing agencies even after an offence has been committed.'.
Answer: (d) SQRP.
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Rearrange the jumbled parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.

P: similar contents to earn more revenues
Q: the theatre management appreciated
R: the popularity of such themes
S: and emphasised staging plays with
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the subject, then the verb, then the rest.
Step 1: Join the parts to read: 'The theatre management appreciated the popularity of such themes and emphasised staging plays with similar contents to earn more revenues.'.
Answer: (a) QRSP.
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Rearrange the jumbled parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.

P: the supreme court in its majesty
Q: Article 21 which deals with the right to life
R: and magnanimity has expounded
S: profoundly the semantic sweep of
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the subject, then the verb, then the rest.
Step 1: Join the parts to read: 'The supreme court in its majesty and magnanimity has expounded profoundly the semantic sweep of Article 21 which deals with the right to life.'.
Answer: (d) PRSQ.
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Rearrange the jumbled parts P, Q, R and S to form a meaningful sentence.

P: of unpopular policies or a discredited leader or government
Q: one of these is that in focussing on the legitimacy of a political
R: in which political authority is challenged as a result
S: regime or system of rule tells us little about the circumstances
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the subject, then the verb, then the rest.
Step 1: Join the parts to read: 'One of these is that in focussing on the legitimacy of a political regime or system of rule tells us little about the circumstances in which political authority is challenged as a result of unpopular policies or a discredited leader or government.'.
Answer: (d) QSRP.
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom or phrase.

I always preferred to study Physics and Mathematics, now choosing Economics and Literature for further studies is another __kettle of fish__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: 'Another kettle of fish' means an entirely different matter.
Step 2: Option (b) says 'slightly', which weakens the idiom; the answer is (a).
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom or phrase.

He criticised the participants for __sitting on the fence__ and not contributing in finalising the report.
questions.opt_d: Showing no respect to the Chair
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: To sit on the fence is to avoid taking a side or making a decision.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom or phrase.

He __strained every nerve__ to understand the discourse on Philosophy.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: To strain every nerve is to try as hard as possible.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom or phrase.

When it comes to using technology, she is completely __at sea__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: To be at sea is to be confused or bewildered.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom or phrase.

He is not a great scholar but he has the __gift of the gab__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: The gift of the gab is a natural ability to speak fluently and persuasively.
Step 2: Of the options only (c) and (d) are about speaking; (d) 'speak confidently' is the closer match to fluent speech. Treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom or phrase.

This car belonged to Ravi, but recently it __changed hands__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: To change hands is to pass to a new owner.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom or phrase.

He turned down the new assignment; he felt that he already had too many __irons in the fire__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: To have many irons in the fire is to be busy with many tasks at once.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom or phrase.

Something should be done to stop __the brain drain__ of Indian scientists to other countries.
questions.opt_a: Movement of professionals to another country for higher studies
questions.opt_b: Movement of professionals to another country for better prospect
questions.opt_c: Movement of professionals to another country for security
questions.opt_d: Movement of professionals to another country for excursion
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: Brain drain is the emigration of skilled people to other countries for better prospects.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom or phrase.

I just need to take rest and then I’ll be __as right as rain__.
questions.opt_a: To be in good mental and physical state
questions.opt_c: To be able to recall the past events
questions.opt_d: To be able to work for long-hours
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: To be as right as rain is to be perfectly well.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom or phrase.

__It is all Greek to me__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Idiom.
Step 1: 'It is all Greek to me' means I cannot understand it.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__You should__ (a) __read the newspaper regularly__ (b) __to be update with current affairs.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: After 'to be' the participle 'updated' (or 'up to date') is needed, not 'update'.
Step 2: Part (c) is wrong.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Our grandparents__ (a) __will be visited__ (b) __by us this weekend.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: 'We will visit our grandparents this weekend' becomes 'Our grandparents will be visited by us this weekend'.
Step 2: There is no error.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__However, the task is from done,__ (a) __particularly in ensuring equity in__ (b) __the distribution of quality education.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: The phrase is 'far from done', not 'from done'.
Step 2: Part (a) is wrong.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__Looking ahead, the university__ (a) __is expunging revenue generation__ (b) __opportunities to add more facilities for students and staff.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: To expunge is to erase. The sense is that the university is 'exploring' or 'expanding' opportunities, so 'expunging' is wrong.
Step 2: Part (b) is wrong.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Find the part of the sentence that has an error. If there is no error, choose (d).

__If you are interested in__ (a) __applying for the job, your application__ (b) __must received by Friday.__ (c) No error. (d)
questions.explanation:
Concept: Spot the grammatical error.
Step 1: After the modal 'must' the passive needs 'be received'.

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: S1 and S6 are fixed. Arrange P, Q, R and S in between so that the six sentences form a coherent passage.

S1: Mutations are random changes to the base sequence of genes.
S6: Several mutations must occur in the same cell for it to become a tumour cell.
P: This is why mutations in them can result in uncontrolled cell division and therefore tumour formation.
Q: The few genes that can become cancer-causing after mutating are known as oncogenes.
R: Most genes do not cause cancer if they mutate.
S: In a normal cell oncogenes are involved in the control of cell cycle and cell division.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: R (most genes are harmless) follows S1; Q introduces oncogenes; S says what oncogenes do normally; P ('This is why...') gives the consequence.
Step 2: Order: R Q S P.
Answer: (a) RQSP.

R: One such most popular program is Word Processor.
S: When computers have affected our life styles and work patterns, this activity is also not left out.
questions.explanation:

Step 1: S links writing with computers; Q mentions application programs; R names the word processor as one such; P describes what it provides.

S1: There exists a close relationship between meteorology and climatology.
S6: First, the meteorological aspect of this discipline examines the process of gain and loss of heat energy by the air layer near the ground, keeping in view the fact that the basic principles apply at any place on the globe. Second, climatological aspect of the discipline examines the global pattern of thermal environment.
P: In other words, it is concerned with the study of the characteristics and behaviour of the atmosphere.
Q: The function of climatology is two-fold.
R: Climatology, on the other hand, is concerned with the discussion of the component elements of climate as well as the factors which determine and control its distribution.
S: Meteorology, the physics of the lower atmosphere, studies the individual phenomenon of the atmosphere.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Find the opening idea, then follow the links (this, also, however).
Step 1: S defines meteorology; P restates it ('In other words'); R contrasts climatology ('on the other hand'); Q says the function of climatology is two-fold, which S6 explains ('First...Second...').

Answer: (a) SPRQ.

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He accepted the car ______ his claim for ₹50,000.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'In lieu of' means in place of; the car replaced the money claim.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

I’ll phone you sometime ______ the afternoon.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: Parts of the day take 'in': 'in the afternoon'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He raised several questions ______ the future of the organisation.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'Concerning' acts as a preposition meaning about.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

He is the gentleman whose name is written ______ the board.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: Writing on a surface takes 'on': 'written on the board'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

______ his negligence the company suffered a heavy loss.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'On account of' gives the reason: the loss was due to his negligence.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

______ the resistance offered by the culprit, he was arrested by the police.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: He was arrested despite the resistance; 'notwithstanding' means in spite of.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

______ his illness, he could not finish the work on time.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'As a consequence of' is the correct phrase; 'in consequence to' and 'subsequent for' are wrong, and 'on account' needs 'of'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the most appropriate word or group of words for the blank.

______ rope ladders they scaled the wall.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Choose the word that fits grammar and meaning.
Step 1: 'By means of' shows the instrument used to scale the wall.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

He is diligent; therefore ______.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Therefore' introduces the result of diligence, so he will succeed.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

A bomb went off in the city centre, but fortunately ______.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'But fortunately' signals good news: nobody was hurt.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Each of the scholars ______.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Each' takes a singular verb: 'has done well'.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

He asked whether either of the brothers ______.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Either of the brothers' is singular, and the reported clause stays in the past: 'was at home'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

One cannot be too careful of ______.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: The subject 'One' needs the matching 'one’s'.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

The applicant is the native of this country, so he has the right ______.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'The right to vote' is the standard pattern.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

No sooner had he returned ______.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'No sooner' is followed by 'than'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

Fortunately the news ______.
questions.opt_a: wasn’t as bad as we expected
questions.opt_b: weren’t as bad as we expected
questions.opt_c: couldn’t as bad as we expected
questions.opt_d: happened with as bad as we expected
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'News' is singular, so 'wasn’t as bad as we expected'.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

When I was on holiday, ______.
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Luggage' is uncountable and takes a singular verb; 'all my luggage was stolen' is the only correct form.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: Choose the option that best completes the sentence.

I got up very early, ______.
questions.opt_a: but Jack got up much before
questions.opt_b: but Jack got up even before
questions.opt_c: but Jack got up earlier to me
questions.opt_d: but Jack got up even earlier
questions.explanation:
Concept: Complete the sentence logically and grammatically.
Step 1: 'Even earlier' correctly compares Jack's time with mine.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: What is the writers’ idea of ‘truth’ in the paragraph?
questions.opt_b: Truth can be told and avoided conveniently
questions.opt_d: Truth may be a choice of ancient Grecians
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The writer says that once found, truth 'imposeth upon man’s thoughts', so it can be a compulsion.
Step 2: The passage does not link truth with divinity or say it can be avoided at will. Treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Why do men love lies?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage says men love lies neither for pleasure nor for advantage but 'for the lie’s sake'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Which metaphor is used in the passage to compare the value of truth and lies?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: Truth is compared to a pearl that shows best by day and a lie-mixed pleasure to a diamond that shows best in varied lights.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: What literary device does the author use when he says, “truth is naked”?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: Giving truth a human quality (nakedness) is personification.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: What would happen if truths were not mixed with lies?
questions.opt_a: There would not be any pleasure in the pursuit of truth
questions.opt_b: Truth would be clear and undiluted
questions.opt_c: Lies would no longer be necessary
questions.opt_d: The beauty of truth would shine forth
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The author says 'a mixture of a lie doth ever add pleasure', so without the mixture there would be less pleasure.
Step 2: The passage does not say truth would shine more; treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: According to the author, legal literacy
questions.opt_a: needs to be interpreted and understood in consonance with elements of social custom and justice
questions.opt_b: needs to be interpreted and understood in consonance with elements of economic and psychological factors and law
questions.opt_c: needs to be interpreted and understood in terms of unjust existence of human being and justice
questions.opt_d: needs to be interpreted and understood in consonance with elements of environmental conservation and law
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage says legal literacy must cover state law, custom and the community, and ends by asking how far it gives us resources of justice.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: As a citizen one is supposed to
questions.opt_a: make a balance between the legal aspects and cultural existence
questions.opt_b: give a priority to our cultural existence
questions.opt_c: give a priority to constitutional provisions
questions.opt_d: know that knowledge about constitutional regulation is an impediment to cultural existence
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage says we must know both state law and community norms and decide which obligation has precedence when they collide, which means balancing them.
Answer: (a).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: The above passage deals in
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The passage keeps returning to 'legal literacy' and what it requires.
Answer: (b).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: According to the writer ‘diverse combinatory prowess’ means
questions.opt_a: A process of evolving a legal and constitutional system of cohesive elements.
questions.opt_b: A provision of evolving a law of customary practices by avoiding constitutional provisions
questions.opt_c: A provision of evolving constitutional laws by neglecting customary practices
questions.opt_d: A process of combining contrasting elements into a competent legal mechanism
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: The phrase refers to the law working as constitution confronting custom and custom confronting constitution, that is, as a combination of both.
Step 2: (d) 'combining contrasting elements into a competent legal mechanism' is the nearest. Treat this item as low-confidence.
Answer: (d).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)

questions.subject: Reading Comprehension
questions.question: Which among the following is closest in meaning to the word ‘resistance’?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Use only what the passage says.
Step 1: Resistance is opposition to authority; the closest option is 'defiance'.
Answer: (c).
questions.source: CDS II 2023 English set A (set code JNUP-U-ENG – A)
